features.note: Attempt-1 failure resolved: three distinct blade volumes read across the two views. Top blade shows its lit upper face with a folded leading edge tipped toward the viewer (+theta) while the blade below it presents a narrow opposite-slanted face (-theta), so counter-rotation reads mid-travel; the bottom blade is the weakest read (a foreshortened strip near the bottom rail) but is confirmed in the orbit view.

Attempt-1 flush-mount failure resolved: a plated spindle now protrudes from the frame right face across a clearly visible air gap (proportion consistent with >=37 mm free spindle) and the orange body is socketed on it with a dark clamp collar at entry. The anti-rotation strap does not read distinctly — the lower bearing-end pin visually overlaps the actuator's lower edge in the spec view — which caps the score at threshold. The two small plated bearing-end pins flanking the drive stub are much thinner and shorter than the clamped spindle, so they cause only minor confusion, not a second-shaft misread.

Attempt-1 failure resolved: a light circular dial-plate block now sits behind the dark pointer needle on the actuator's outboard face. Printed 0-90 arc is not expected at blockout; 1:1 rotation cannot be verified from stills, judged on pointer + dial blocking, which is now present.
No regression: both views show the channel casing with real depth (~127 mm proportion vs the 600x400 face) and separated flange planes on both faces, including corner tabs.

Attempt-1 occlusion resolved by the -35 deg orbit view: a plated vertical tie rod with three dark crank blocks on the left axle ends reads clearly on the non-actuator side. Coherent motion with the blades cannot be verified from a still; decomposition and placement are correct.

important_features.note: Still no dark edge-strip blocking on blade meeting lines and no jamb strips on the interior side faces in either view; blade edges read as bare light-gray plate edges. Judged leniently at blockout but nothing signals seals.
Attempt-1 failure resolved: a flat white label-plate block is visible on the actuator body in both views; printed text not expected at blockout.
Attempt-1 failure resolved: the cable now leaves the gland and droops with a visible multi-segment curve (clearer in the orbit view) instead of a straight rigid rod.

defects: Blade-seal blocking is absent: no thin dark strips along blade meeting edges and no jamb strips on the opening's interior sides in either view — this is the sole remaining gate failure (important_average 0.63 < 0.65).

Anti-rotation strap is not distinctly readable: in the spec view the thin lower bearing-end pin overlaps the actuator's lower edge, and no separate slotted strap block from actuator underside to frame can be confirmed.

The two plated bearing-end pins on the frame right face flanking the drive stub could be mistaken for extra shafts at a glance; they stay subordinate to the thick clamped spindle but add mild visual noise near the mount.
The bottom blade reads only as a narrow foreshortened strip near the bottom rail in both views — present but the weakest of the three blades.
Dial plate has no 0-90 arc marking yet (acceptable at blockout; record for the materials pass).
Mechanical: draws=0 is an N/A placeholder — blender track has no draw-call probe; do not read it as a real draw count.
corrections: Add thin near-black (EPDM #101012) edge strips along the meeting edges of all three blades and vertical jamb strips on both interior side faces of the opening — this alone recovers the important_average above 0.65.

Make the anti-rotation strap read: a flat slotted strap block from the actuator underside to the frame right face, offset in Z from the bearing-pin line so it does not visually merge with the lower bearing end.
Shorten or thin the two bearing-end pins (or darken them) so the clamped drive stub stays visually dominant on the right face.

mechanical.note: blender track: draws=0 is an N/A marker (no draw-call probe); 1152 tris, well within 400k budget
